I remembered my mother's words, and drawn in by the tavern's promise of ale and a good time, I stepped inside. The old mariner was polishing a glass as I walked in. I told him I was out of coins, but I tossed him a pearl from Orville. He prepared a beer and a tale right away.

In a hushed voice, he reminisced about the week he'd spent inside the maw of a beached sea dragon while stranded far away, his voice rough as the water outside the window. He said he hid between its pearly teeth and slept under its tongue, making a pyre atop its skull to signal rescuers.

Then, he abruptly stopped. I asked him how the story ended, and he quietly held out his hand for another payment. I'll return soon to hear the rest!

Back in the day, I was a rowdy lad. I'd spent each school day by the beach instead of on the classroom bench, kicking strangers' sand castles and skipping rocks on the water.

Once, I spotted a small boat in the distance, with a shadowy figure balancing on it. As I focused my attention there, their shapes toppled and morphed into one, disturbing the water around. Did someone slip into the lake? I waited to see the person resurface, but no one emerged.

Moments later, a creature made from seaweed and saltwater rose from beneath the rippling waves by the shore. It was much closer than the boat had been, and as it neared, I began to spot a graying face below the heap of algae. It was the captain.

I asked him how he was able to cross the waters between the sinking ship and the beach so quickly. He smiled, and said: "A mermaid's kiss gave me fins, dear boy!" and trotted off.

Only later did I notice that his feet had left a strange imprint in the sand. Could his story have been true?

p.n: The Lies Of A Wizened Man
p.t:
Back in my school days, I was taught that Captain Melville liked to tell stories. Tall ones. The kind of tales that smell more like old boots than truth. As a working man, I’ve always known his tavern, "Ol’ Salt ’N Pepper", was named not just for his sea-worn beard, but because you’re supposed to take everything he says with a pinch, nay, a load of salt.

And yet, people lap it up.

They crowd around him like he’s some sea-born prophet, hanging on every crooked word. Why? The man’s a liar. A fossil. He hasn’t been out past the bay in years. Why trust a word he says — even worse, why buy his fish? Especially when we sell better catch, cheaper, and without the song and dance!

Just last week, he burst into the square, hair all tangled, shouting, "The Drak! I saw 'em, they're back!" Theatrics. Always theatrics with him.

It’s just another one of his tales, spun for coin and glory. And yet, folks eat it up.
Fools, the lot of 'em.

Once, as a seamstress, I had quite the popular customer — the old Captain himself!

I will never forget the dawn at which he stumbled through my open doors, beard not nearly as ashen as it is today, little more than a stained shirt on his body.
"Morn', young lass!" He cawed with a hoarse voice, "I'd like a new coat! Deep blue as the sea, with gold and glamor, I'd say — hick!"

While taking his measurements, I observed him closely. He smelled of wine and was missing not only his coat, but one shoe... When I asked him about it, he said:
"Nay, the wine is half the story — See, as I was out late on the canal, an old devil born from the frothing blue called to me from below! He said he'd trade me a bottle of his finest for one button of my coat! A bottle for a button? I thought: Why not? But as I reached down to receive the wine, the impish creature pulled me in by my cufflinks and turned back seafoam! Hick! I went overboard, mayday, mayday! They had to fish me and my boat out — and my coat, it was gone with the waves! Hick!"

I had his new jacket ready within three days, but I always wondered how his old clothes didn't wash ashore. Did they turn into seafoam, too?

Reports were right
The "Drak" are near 
I've never seen something like this
They're waiting in the thicket, salivating

Joshua and Powell are gathering the divers and some of the younglings who can hold their breath
Only way out is through the water
No air stops possible — they might spot us

We hide out in the shipwrecks by the shore
Powell is taking the Mining Sieve
Sharp enough in case of an emergency
Ancients keep us safe

- Rolf

It has come to our attention that some individuals have attempted to manually clear blockages in the grinder while the machinery is still in operation. We must emphasize that this practice is strictly prohibited due to the severe safety risks involved, including the potential for loss of limbs, or worse, loss of employment.

Under no circumstances should any part of the body be placed near or within moving equipment. 
If access to the millstone is absolutely necessary, all water flow must be completely stopped prior to any intervention. To stop water flow, close the water gates in the waterwheel's basin.This will ensure the external water wheel ceases operation and that all related machinery is fully disabled.

Please treat this matter with the utmost seriousness. Your safety is our highest priority.

Sincerely,
Timberwolf Logging & Co.
Safety & Operations Team

Ever since the company ramped up production, I’ve noticed something off about the water. 
There's a strange motion in the current. An unnatural one — heavier, slower. A purple haze dances at the edge of my vision whenever I focus my eyes on the stream.

I used to drink from it without a second thought. We all did.

Now, we’ve been strongly discouraged from drinking the river water. Management says it’s “a precaution,” but Timberwolf Logging & Co. started offering bottled water themselves — for a price. Not up front, of course. They just dock it from our pay. Quietly, automatically. Like it’s part of the cost of doing business.

I keep thinking: if I can’t drink from the land I work, if I have to buy water from the same people possibly spoiling it, what kind of freedom is that? What kind of future?

Location: Submerged Temple Ruins – Coordinates Confirmed
Estimated Dive Time: 008 Hours, surfacing possible

Pre-Dive Briefing

Time: Before dusk. Docking went smoothly despite dense growths and scattered debris below.
Place: Abandoned, half-swallowed by the lake. Ideal for exploration!

Observing the parameters of the ruin confirms earlier reports. Multiple moss-ridden stairwells lay upwards, toward the gaping mouth of the temple. Structural integrity is questionable. Best we make good time and beat our own record!

I'm sure we'll find the first chamber as described by the previous team: waterlogged, more seaweed than stone, sealing the flooded pathways beyond. A mechanism or puzzle kept them from breaching the tunnels. That’s where we come in!

The team’s solid. Spirits are high. I’ve got confidence in Edd Exley — he’s sharp, steady, and knows how to handle tight spaces. 

Timing’s crucial. We’ll begin the descent at first light. With luck, the sun will be high enough to pierce through the grates and mark the resurfacing zones. 

We won't skip breakfast prep, though. Caught a few fish en route; they’ll be fine once roasted!

p.n: Special Operation – Diver's Log – Entry 033 – Shit!
p.t:
Location: You know where!!
Estimated Dive Time: Too damn long

Post Dive Findings

Time: It's dark out. No light. 
Place: No sign of Edd.

Last seen: He hit the first checkpoint, the metal grates by the overgrown terrace, behind time. Seemed winded, but steady. I thought about pulling him out. I should've stopped the mission then. Pried open the bars. Lifted him up and out of those treacherous waters.

I didn't.

The sun has set, which means Edd will have trouble finding his scheduled resurfacing spots.
Estimated dive time has been exceeded.

I think he has air for... maybe thirty more minutes, if he doesn't panic. It won't last for the way back.

We're running from grate to grate, lighting torches, yelling his name, trying to signal a safe spot to surface. But below, everything is pitch black. The deep swallows both sound and light.

I wonder if he can even still tell up from down. I wonder if he's scared. Alone. Cold. I wonder if he knows he'll die... I wonder if he'll still try to make it to the end.

For Crew & Loaders

INCOMING / OUTGOING CARGO:

Princess Sue (ETA: Tuesday)
- Load 12 crates (nails & lumber) from Left-Hand Storage Room

Dainty Beluga (Arriving Today – Short Layover)
- Transfer grain sacks directly upon arrival

Oceanwasp (ETA: Unknown)
- Small vessel. Special Order: 1x Handpan – Currently on elevator platform (Note: Platform stuck again – maintenance needed ASAP)

Gormander's Seascaper (Awaiting arrival – date TBD)
- Needs, and I quote: "As many coffee beans as the damn thing will hold – I have a kingdom to run here!"
- Additional materials to be stored until arrival. Right-Hand Storage Room.
- Dave & Darrel assigned to storage handling

NOTE:
Anyone seen Dave or Darrel lately? They’re supposed to be managing storage, but haven’t been spotted on the dock in days. If found, send ‘em our way.

– Dock Office

Can't meet ya today
Dock office posted a notice about us. Did ya see it?

Don't worry
I'll be active on the docks, loud and sweaty — lookin' hard and hard at work — gonna cover us for a week or so.

In the meantime, nab some coffee from the Seascaper shipment before we load 'er up! I got a coffee grinder somewhere at home. Some coffee is bound to make our little breaks much sweeter!

DAVE

The text is scribbled in pencil, with faint grease smudges on the edges.

Water’s gettin’ murkier by the day. Not just dirty — wrong. Smells like metal and rot had a baby.

Last order from up top was to “reduce leakage” from the  fluorescent goop into the basin. Doesn’t sound like a plan so much as a prayer... and once that's over, we're done here for good. No lift, no jobs, no pay. Just silence and the smell of rot. 

Until then, we’re setting up grates and stacking grain sacks. Feels like we’re emptying half the silo just to plug a hole. It’s all makeshift. Temporary. And deep down, I don’t think anyone believes it’ll hold. 

I know a farmer in Driftwood Wake. Far enough away from this mess. Water there is still clean... for now. I'll try my luck there. Maybe being in nature will help with this nasty cough I got.

—J

p.n: The Luscious Drakonian Maid, Chapter 2: River Maiden
p.t:
Lush'Kyss: 
I beg thee, Sir Lancehart, avert thine eyes! As my form lies bare before thee under the moonlight's embrace, thine gaze fills me with shame!

Sir Lancehart:
Not shame, but desire swells in thee, my little Lush! Thine flushed strawberry cheeks betray thee!

Lush'Kyss: 
Don't step closer! My waters run so deep and warm, they may swallow thee so and lock thee away until the golden glow of morn!

Sir Lancehart:
So locked away I must be! Sweep me under thine waves, for my heart yearns for naught more than to be held firm beneath thee, to gaze up at the crescent and the supple bosom it illuminates!

Lush'Kyss: 
Oh, to join me in this river's dance wild and free, Sir Lancehart, thine spirit must truly be unchained — but must thee prod me so below with thine appetite?

Sir Lancehart:
Dearest Lush, what thee feels beneath is my lance's tip, to keep us safe whilst we drown in pleasure. I never set forth without protection!

Lush'Kyss: 
Oh, how considerate! One should always bring such wards!

p.n: The Luscious Drakonian Maid, Chapter 3: Beneath Cloth
p.t:
Sir Lancehart: 
Dearest Lush, this disguise will serve thee well. The human garb hides thine emerald scales — with this, all shall see thee as a common milkmaid! Only I will know the truth of thine pure heart and exotic curves!

Lush'Kyss: 
You wish to leave the cover of the canopy together, and live unbound from hate and prejudice... but this cloth is woven of lies! None shall accept me as I hide my deepest desires!

Sir Lancehart:
Do not discard your disguise, Lush'Kyss! We've strayed too far from the thicket! Say, how will thee suffer when a stranger's gaze finds thine flower?

Lush'Kyss: 
Then they may marvel at its divinity! These covers are chains I must break to rid myself of shame! See my claws run across my trembling chest, unabashed! Oh, how would I hide a racing heart such as this, my beloved? Each beat compels me ever forward and into thine embrace! Come, soothe my craving as you did by the silver riverside!

Sir Lancehart:
Thine garden has blossomed, dear! Oh, fire overtakes me! I must wet my lips with thine nectar to quench the thirst!

Lush'Kyss: 
Plant your seed, my beloved! You have my explicit and verbal consent!

Sir Lancehart:
...And I'd never lay a hand on thee with ambiguity overshadowing our bond, as I hold thee in too high a regard!

I despised working at the Cargo Lift. Turns out, I loathe being a farmhand even more.

I still remember when we got shut down as the Shroud-infected water spread to our upper canals. Dragging sandbags around and building makeshift barricades to "ensure water purity" downstream, all while enduring this rotting stench. 

Then, poof: No lift, no work, and I was stuck with a scratchy throat. My new life on the farm is lonesome as hell. The cough and birds around were my only company... 'til yesterday.

While tilling, I saw something shuffle through the trees. The thing was so crooked, I thought it was some sort of beast. Then, bang! Thunder! Lightning! A strange bird's coo! I was distracted by the ruckus above, and when I looked back at the thing, it had moved closer. 

No longer hiding behind a tree line, it revealed itself as a hunched-over hag, cawing: "Your cough is bad, my boy — but you're in luck! I'm an herbalist. Come by my hut, and let my healing tinctures soothe you."
As if on cue, a flight of birds near me took off and soared past. Had to shield my face and all, so close were they! Moments later, the birds and crone were gone. 

I'll go see her tomorrow. Got nothing left to lose.
—J

Once upon a time, there lived a little princess with rosy cheeks and ashen hair, who loved nothing more than playing by the castle pond with her golden ball.

One day, the ball slipped from her hands and sank beneath the water. Distraught, the princess wept until a voice croaked from the reeds:
"Do not cry, little princess. I shall fetch your golden ball — for a kiss from your cherry lips!"

The girl looked up to see a lumpy frog upon a lily pad. Though repulsed, she nodded, yearning for her treasure back. The creature dove in and returned with the ball — but once the princess reclaimed her toy, she fled into the castle without so much as a thank-you.

That night, the frog came knocking on the gates. The king, upon hearing his daughter's promise, insisted she honor her word. But the princess proved reluctant evermore, and overcome by desperation, she threw the pest against a wall. 
As the pale green frog splattered against the bricks, the curse that bound him was broken, and he was freed from the shackles of his cold-blooded form. Born anew, he revealed himself to be a prince.

And so, as is custom, the underage princess was wed to a grown stranger who had tricked her into a kiss — but he was quite handsome, so all was well.

My cousin Rolf is missing!
He went to Orville to work as a pearl diver but never returned.

Rolf may have been a daredevil, but he'd always send word whenever he'd run off!

To anyone who's seen him: let me know where he is or bring him back home! 

- Willy

People 'round 'ere are worried. First, t'was Stillwater Bay, then Goldrock Saddle. We've lost sight of our settlements one by one, and those who make the journey North-West wash ashore like dead fish.
The lads from the ol' lumber mill 'ave family n' friends workin' as divers down in Orville, but none 'ave seen 'em as of late. They've sent neither word nor pearls. They're already gone, I say!

I told 'em not to take lodgings in the valleys. I did. But none listened. Did they all forget the tales?

Many years ago, 'fore the crown got shattered into three, no, 'fore the kingdom had formed at all, we were ambushed.
Wild beasts, half man, half animal, rushed from the coast to darken their waters with our blood, they did. They were envious of our bond with the Ancients, whom they believed to be messengers of their gods. 'Twas a wonder of human engineering n' strategy that we ever defeated 'em.

Today, most of us moved on — but the Drak never forgot. I believe they've returned, I do, but no one listens to an ol' bag o' bones.

I was always proud of my intuition. Could spot those itching for mutiny before they'd ever stepped onto my boat, sensed a storm brewin' from the cry of the gulls miles away.

But this time, just once, could I be wrong?
When I heard the west winds whistle a new tune, did I mistake its sharpness as sinister?
When I reeled in a hundred fish with torn fins, did I misread their injury as a threat?
When I thought I saw the evil doers of old childhood stories leap from the pages into the water, were my eyes betraying me?

Am I spinning a yarn from my own sanity's thread? I ought to warn the others, lest I unravel fully.
Whether they will trust the word of a tale-teller, I cannot say. Some may claim a fisher ought to stick to fishin'...

Lately, Maynard has made a habit of bathing during his break. 

I don't mind so much — I prefer him smelling of rosewater and candlewax to his usual grime and gruff. But he takes HOURS in there, leaving me alone to herd the poor sods in the cells! 

He thinks he's such a sly fox, too — as if I don't see the book he hides under his towel whenever he sets off. I don't care what smut he reads, but can't he hurry with it?

Been a lighthouse keeper for ages. Born and raised on these shores, and proud of it, too.

The sea knows me better than my own mother. Over the years, the ripples in the water imprinted on my face, carved longing lines into my skin as I aged. My visage and story are naught but a map of the great, wide blue.
But today, I thought I spotted something... new.

It was a bright evening, clear as can be. The waters were calm under the setting sun, but I knew not to trust them. Dark clouds gathered on the horizon, foretelling a storm... and underneath them, for just a moment in the far distance, I saw something rise from below. 
A single shade against the shifting background, reaching up like a periscope, watching the shore. Watching us.
Then, it dove out of sight, disappearing from the view of my binoculars. 

It could have been driftwood. Yes, it must've been...

This month, we've lost more ships at sea than we ever did throughout my entire life.

I blame myself, though I know I've always upheld my duty. Every night, I light our fire to signal the safety of our harbor... I stay up, watching the pyre, stoking the flames, choking the smoke to leave only a bright merigold light... but it is not enough, and I'm losing sleep. 

Nightmares rip me from bed, force me to find my binoculars and nightgown, and make me stumble to the platform above amid darkness and rain. I thought, if I stared out long enough, I would see it. See what's causing this. Understand it. Beat it.

The storm clouds are drawing closer, and they're hiding something from me.

The storm finally reached us, waves frothing with hatred and lashing at our shores.

Standing on the lighthouse platform, I felt the gusts rip at my beard and coat. I must still have salt embedded in my skin from that night's winds.

The light inside my covered oil lamp flickered, locked in a fearful dance, twisting and shifting in an effort not to be snuffed out... a repetitive plea with no one to listen, an act soaked in vain, not unlike my own.

Light the fire. Stoke the flames. Wipe down the binoculars. Look out. Light the fire again. It was pointless. The storm smothered all light.
I helplessly held on to the railing, gazing out at the night. That's when I saw it.
Rolling hills, not made of water, but made of countless bodies, rising and falling with the storm's rhythm. A wave to end us. A wave to crush us. A wave to dye the ocean red. A wave of Drak.

I dropped my binoculars and picked up my boots. If this were our death sentence, I would not die a lighthousekeeper.

Something has awoken, I fear.

More people go missing each eve... first, t'was only those who ventured past the bay. But now, anyone too close to the canals during a moonless night is lost to the waters.

I feel like something is testing us... biting down to see if we flinch, fight, or flee. But what can we do in the face of a nameless specter that's come with a challenge? There are no guards, no lord left to defend us... They've set off to fight a holy war and left us behind, near dark waters hiding sinister fates. 

Some people chose to move further inland. Even the lighthousekeeper has fled, or so I heard. An old man who spent his entire life by this coast... I wonder what he saw last night, during that sunless storm... and how long we have until it reveals itself.

p.n: Harbor Log, Day 12 of Yearwake, 503 D.A.— Personal Notes
p.t:
The crown sent word.
We ought to prepare a new vessel for its maiden voyage, but the ship’s to be sent off with cargo none of us are allowed to inspect. Strange business. Crates bear no marks, no writs, no tally for the ledger... and they're sealed shut.

The Lord deems them of such weight that his own men were dispatched to see them stowed. Thought I’d see sharp-eyed veterans, but the lot that stumbled in yesterday looked half-dead, eyes glazed and dragging their boots. They’re fixing cannons to a merchant hull... my hull. Never seen the like. 

I know not the purpose of this lading, only that it sits ill with me. Shouldn't I know what shipments come and go like the back of my hand?

p.n: Harbor Log, Day 13 of Yearwake, 503 D.A.— Abandon Ship!!
p.t:
I gave in to my suspicion tonight and slipped aboard the vessel. The soldiers had turned their backs, staring off into the distance, fixated on a point beyond the horizon... unmoving. It was the perfect time to strike.

A dockmaster ought to know what passes through his harbor, no matter whose seal it bears, I say! So I snuck into the cargo hold, careful not to let the iron grate cover slip from my trembling hands. The air below smelled rotten. Infested. Could it be rats, or some dead stowaway? I covered my nose and mouth with a handkerchief and pressed on, making my way to the back of the hold where the crates were stacked.

Once there, I broke one's seal and recoiled at the sight that revealed itself before me.
The cases were not filled with grain or powder, but with some choking fog — sealed inside like a thing alive, pressing against its confines, rebelling. No markings, no warning. Just a pale mist festering on a bed of foul mushroom flesh.

Does the Lord seek to spread a sickness to distant shores? My vessels should ship food and clothing, not a new form of warfare crueler than steel! 
I am resigning tomorrow... may the next sod bear witness to what comes next.

...We're out of coffee, so if you're looking to come in and relax, the best we can offer is tea.

We may have a spare machine in the attic, but the top levels of the tower need repairs, so it's not safe to ascend. Of course, if anyone out there is willing to risk their life for it, we'll promise free coffee for the foreseeable future.

Best of luck!

lore.n: The Alchemy Of Bean And Water

p.t:
One for tough warriors:

Take roasted beans, ground fine as dust,
and mingle them with hot water.
Let the brew be dark and bitter — a strong potion
to rouse the spirit and quicken the mind.

Brew the ground beans in water as is custom,
then soften the brew with milk until the bitterness fades.

The result: a smooth, warm, and pleasant cup
I'd like to call this creation: Latte

A sweet comfort in weary hours:

Grind the beans and steep them in water —
add sugar, that the flavor be full and kind

A Sweet Mokka is prepared.

The swimming pool's draining system has been acting up again. Whenever I try to lower the water levels, it takes ages for the flow to subside... It's like the tunnels below are blocked again.
I told myself I’d call in a technician, but truth be told, I’ve been putting it off. The men cling to that pool like it’s the last scrap of home we’ve got out here. Taking it away, even for repairs, would break morale in half.

And yet… there’s something off. A sound, low and constant, like stones shifting under the waterline. Probably a stone or a dead rat, bumping against the pipes. It's probably nothing. Just grit in the filters, I bet. But every night, when the rumble rouses me awake, I can’t shake the thought that something's down there.

Upon examining these Drak inscriptions, my analysis is as follows:

Tribal Structure:

The Drak hardly consider themselves as a unified species or culture, instead preferring increasingly insular and tribal groupings despite sharing a common language root and build.
Over the course of generations, these divisions have led to distinct scale patterns, color morphologies, dialectical shifts, and unique cultural practices — notably, a preference for different holy idols/ sages/ war heroes that shape their understanding of self, and are titular to their tribal variation.
Tribes lay claim to different domains geographically, locked in an interracial territorial conflict whenever the brood's expansion demands it.

The Drak'Dal, for example, are named for their idol, Dalszul, and currently contest the archipelago offshore alongside the Drak'Mer; followers of Merphisz. This conflict has seemingly begun after the Drak'Dal were driven out of the Veilwater Basin. 

Other notable tribes include:
Drak'Ari, followers of Arisztar
Drak'Fyr, followers of Fyraszh

The differences between these creatures are to be contextualized not as natural variance, but as the markings of a common gene pool, split apart into new and isolated strands carried by the tribes. 
Said isolation, alongside constant interracial conflict and assumed increased rates of inbreeding, may explain the perceived cognitive and linguistic degeneration of the Drak.

Cultural and linguistic degeneration: 
The Drak texts recovered from more recent layers of sediment — often dredged from coastal waters or shipwrecks — tend to exhibit simpler structures, reduced vocabulary, and degraded syntax when compared to earlier samples unearthed in local temples. This suggests a loss of linguistic complexity over time.

It appears that the trajectory of their societal evolution may have stagnated — or even regressed. Additionally, if I interpret correctly, it is to be assumed that they hold a grudge or a somewhat natural aversion to technological advancements and engineering. They perceive most modern human inventions as admissions of weakness rather than solutions. Further research is required.

(The engravings are delicate, and each stroke seems carefully placed. A plaque at the bottom reads: Example of advanced Drak writing, reclaimed from a flooded temple. Presumed age: over 1000 years old)

Hail Vesztah, the great Broodmother.

She, who grew from a single droplet of blood.
She, who rose from the sea of chaos in the eye of the storm.

She, who wove the waves for Merphisz.

She, who ignited the heart of Fyraszh.

She, who bestowed wings onto Arisztar.

She, who gifted Dalszul gold and gallows.

She, who is both mother and maw
The womb and the grave
Giver and Destroyer
The great ruler of Ark Morgo

In her womb, we grow
In her lap, we begin
Under her watch, we suffer or succeed
And in her grasp, we shall end

(The writing is crude, and the signs are written with short, apathetic scratches. A plaque reads: Example for rudimentary Drak writing, found by fishers dredging near the archipelago. Presumed age: Recent.)

Drak'Mer weak. Why breed underwater? Lay eggs in ponds? Waste of time.

Dalszul would never. Would build temples. Adorned in gold. Would force humans, brick by brick. 

Young Drak should hatch and stomp their feet! Should stick spears in land that belongs to them! Not splish and splash! 
That's why Drak'Dal strong! Big muscles! Lift stone! Spill blood!

Hail Dalszul! Rah Rah!

Ah, it feels proper to plant my boots back on solid ground! Masquerading as a soldier was an interesting intermission, but dancing with the winds as a glider connoisseur was most thrilling, I believe!

Still, deep down, I remain a humble minstrel — a slave to the melody that bleeds from my aching heart! Yes, I declare: T'was the urge to create that brought me back — so says my newly discovered fear of vultures. They haunt not only the heights 'round my former outpost, but my dreams, as well... no matter!

I've returned to the love of my life: music! And thus, my mistress demands I try my luck at the Lord’s court! I hear the fellow’s got good taste and a sharp tongue for those who offend it. I may either join his banquet, or range of hunting trophies — but worry does not suit me. Besides, danger to a daring bastard is like a raindrop on a rose. 
It simply sweetens the eve.
- "Lucky" Chester Loft

It's the first day of yearfall, 502 D.A. and I've finally reached the castle, and whilst preparing for my little soliloquy, I could not help but let my mind wander! 

How shall I ever memorize my lines whilst dreaming beneath such magnificent architecture? I thought the statues of our Lord that line the town entrance fed my hungry eyes, but it seems they were merely an appetizer! The stonework here holds space for scenery, I say:

These columns reach toward the dome like prayers on a rainy night, coating the citadel in an awe-inspiring serenity. Imagine a gray chapel atop a cliff, moss creeping through the century-old brick. Thunder and lightning haunt not only the sanctuary, but the rivulet choking its precipice.
Stone arcs spring from side to side, frogs leaping across the rippling stream. They span 'round the pilasters like the skeleton of an umbrella, sheltering us sheep from the howling winds.

I must not forget myself! My audience is drawing near — I hope the Lord will savor my voice! If not, I might hang from one such arc soon enough... Focus, Chester! Grim thoughts ought not to be in a blond and pretty head like yours!

— "Lucky" Chester Loft

I’ve been working in the nearby mine every day, but lately, I haven't been able to stop thinking that there might be more to be made from those aquamarine crystals than just hauling them out of the rock. I ground some down with a small grinder and ended up with the finest, most brilliant powder I’ve ever seen.

After mixing it with a few ingredients I had at home, I think I’ve created the perfect pigment. Tomorrow, I’ll prepare a small batch and show it to Casper.

Maybe this is my chance to leave the mine for good. This could be the start of something much bigger.

I am too old now... even tending to the banana plants has become a struggle. I had dreamed of renovating our house, of giving it new life, but my strength is gone.

The building blocks to fix our roof still sit up in the attic, gathering dust. I suppose they will remain there forever, untouched — just like so many of the plans I once had.

And yet... my wife is proud of all that I have already done. That thought brings me comfort. Perhaps it is enough. I am enough.

Dear Supervisor,
I had hoped to write this note respectfully to thank you for the opportunity to work here, but I can’t keep up the pretense anymore. The truth is, this job is breaking me. The labor is too much: day after day of swinging tools until my body gives out, only to collapse into miserable tents that barely shield us. It’s inhuman.

And now, the fog. That damned fog creeps in from the rear shafts. None of us know what it is, but we all feel it. The headaches, the shaking hands, the strange dreams — don't tell me it's nothing because we all know it's not. Some of the men already look like shadows of themselves.

I won't be next. I won't wait until the mine and the fog consume me completely. I quit. Let someone else break their back and lose their mind for you. If the ore is so important to you, you can dig it out yourself.

p.n: My Ancestors And I Grew Up In These Tunnels
p.t:
Our family worked tirelessly to chisel ever-winding shafts into the stone, though all of them are gray and dull. It's hard for me to imagine a different life, lest I gaze at the water nearby and remember my youth.

I remember reading about a mermaid: A lonely maiden whose heart melted into the waves as she turned to seafoam. Years in the mine made me forget, made me grow up. But not all let go of such fairytales.

Once, I met a man with legs that should've been fins. The Siren Seeker, they called him — always caressing the sea as if it were his lover, letting the tide envelop him as he dove for treasures below.
He was collecting sun-bleached seashells by the shore as I asked:
"What do you seek in the water that you can't find on land? Shouldn't you take up proper work and settle down?"

Without looking up, he mumbled through a smile: "I seek the kiss of a mermaid — one who hides her voice in conch shells and words in bottled messages. I'll save her from turning to foam, and me from falling to gray. " 

Today, I recall the Seeker's words, retrace the pages of that fairytale book in my mind. I understand now. Our family worked tirelessly to chisel ever-winding shafts into the stone, all of which are gray and dull. I wish I hadn't forgotten the magic from yonder years. I wish I had carved my own path and set sail.

I have been seeking the secret of eternity for decades now. Each spell I craft, I test upon the restless bones that linger in the shadows. Mindless creatures — yet obedient to my will — serve as my apprentices in this quest.

And yet... My promise of everlasting life eludes me. I leave them where they fall, discarded, silent witness to my genius, or at least my attempts.

It doesn't matter, there are more tombs to explore. With each chamber I edge closer to perfection. The failures are merely stepping stones. I will not cease, for eternity the ruin of all else is worth.

For my next experiment, I’ve heard whispers of a tomb hidden among thick groves of banana plants. From the water, I shall cross Gateway Outpost "Darkwater" and venture into the jungle to seek it out.

The Undying Flame... I thought I was onto something here, but all it does is reduce creatures to ash and bones. Eternity in the afterlife, perhaps, but hardly what I intended.

Adjacent to the large lake with the tower lies Goldrock Saddle, just east of which another tomb should be hidden, the earth arching over it.

I can't believe it! I have created a healing spell — finally! But... it heals others?! Can you believe it? What am I supposed to do with this? What good is it to me if others live longer? .. but at least I am on the right track. The next tomb awaits. I've heard stories of young folk daring to race through it, braving its challenges. Whoever makes it to the other side… well, they live. Its supposed to be close to the Mining Rift towards the Blackmire.

Uff… this one put up a fight. Fast as lightning, we raced through the catacombs. To honor him, I set up a grave right where he drew his last breath…
And now… a Lightning Spell?! I thought I was close. I’m growing tired of this. I believe there is only one last tomb left, near Stillwater Bay towards the foot of the hills...

Hmm… maybe if I cast this spell on myself long enough, I can shock-freeze my body — and then thaw whenever I wish. That way, I could extend my life… right? Right?!
I’ve done it! I made it!

- Till the fields 
- Clean up (get rid of cobwebs!)
- Buy new candles -> grab coins from silver chest?
- Need to fix the basement ladder
- Move wine barrels back into place

Whenever a storm is brewing, I feel the clouds linger atop that nearby Drak'Dal ruin... a strange phenomenon. It's as if the rain and thunder were pulled there, by magnetism or magic.

I always thought lightning never strikes twice, but perhaps I was wrong.

Lightning strikes the olden pillars yonder more frequently, it seems. Does that overgrown hovel bear any artifacts worth uncovering? Or does it simply lie amidst a valley, most curious? Who knows, who knows...

An odd customer came in today. 

Rugged man, tall and morose. A knight of sorts, or mercenary, though I've never seen his insignia here before. Clearly, he had one too many sips of wine already — or grog, I suspect.
He had no gold, so I tried to send 'em away, but it was in vain. Kept slurring his words, eyes wide and bloodshot, pointing at the rum on the topmost shelf with his gloved hand, almost too heavy to hold up straight.

His arms kept sinking to the counter mid-motion, veering about as if his body couldn't keep pace with his demands, or as if his limbs were made from wet sacks of grain.
Aggravated by his own limpness and lack of liquor, he tore off his gauntlets and tossed them across the room, growling. 
I ducked underneath the bar. When I saw his bare hand reach across the counter from below and grip the edge, I feared he might lunge toward me... but instead, he scrambled across, tumbled to the floor, and shuffled to the liquor rack.
He had put the bottle to his lips before crossing the doorstep and shambling back outside. 

His gauntlets are the only trace he left. They seem valuable. I've stored them in the attic for now, should he return with a clearer head and fuller pockets.

There's not much time. Forgive my candor, brother.

1. Gormander poses no threat
His capital is nearly defenseless. No signs of "Ancient weapons" or a conspiracy. The Elixir merely made his ilk plump and greedy, not bloodthirsty... though they've grown paranoid, like most.

2. We've been lied to
That wanderer poisons the mind of our Lord. We cannot trust a word from his forked tongue. 

3. Leave with me
Abandon your post. Join me on my route down south. Turn your back on the war, the Shroud, the death. Wash your hands clean in more peaceful waters.

4. Discard this letter
...Lest you want your sister's blood spilled.

— Athalan

I always had a knack for magic, but I abandoned its path many years ago.
When I was young, I'd often linger near the Lacemaker Pond in the Northeast. The bitter cold didn't bother me, for I was much too focused on the spectacle that unfolded whenever the sorcerers came to train.
With a flick of the wrist, they stitched ice crystals into the air and embroidered the frozen lake with a web of delicate fissures.

One such eve, an adept I didn't recognize leaned too fervently into his cast, clumsily tipping the floe below. A novice, I reckon — weaving northern lights across the sky in one moment and slipping beneath water the next.
I stood at the edge of the pond, waiting for him to resurface, but his soaked spellcasting equipment dragged him from the aurora and into the deep. Had the cold night not pulled me away, I'd be waiting still.

That's how I came to choose a quiet life, engulfed by the warmth of a fire instead of a freezing lake's depths.

- "Drak Slurp"
The classic. Puréed Algae in coconut water or milk.

- "Glorb Sizzle"
Bubbling mudwater enriched with ginger and a wormy surprise!

- "Sweet Sting"
Banana milk and honey. Topped with a crispy bee snack.

- Coconut Water (plain)
... with a little umbrella!

- Water
Carbonated, you animals!

For SNACKS, we got:
- More worms (alive)
- More crispy baked bees (dead)
- Half-incubated eggs (you be the judge of it)
"What is greed if not a pit to drown in?"

Drak'Dal were away for too long. 

All our temples crumble to dust! 
Drak'Dal will show Ancients true strength! Will show that Ancients made a mistake with fleshy humans! Drak'Dal won't build in anyone's shadow! 

Build a new home! Build for Dalszul! Build, or Broodmother Vesztah will have your head!

Rah Rah!

First, there was nothing. The winds and waters were still, the land lay dormant and unclaimed.

But soon, a breeze arose, and the silence crescendoed into a fanfare. A storm cloud, spouting thunder and lightning, spread across the skies — and from its heart began to pour a waterfall of violet blood.

As the droplets laid siege to the wilds below, they tore down every blossom and vine, marking their fragility. The downpour turned the flatlands into a battlefield first, and later, an ocean.

Once weakness was purged, the storm subsided, but the sea of blood left in its wake became a primordial soup that gave rise to a victor in the chaos. The Broodmother Vesztah was born.

She, the first Drak, reigned over all — but sitting lonely on her throne, she spoke, "What is greed if not a pit to drown in? What is dominance without dominion?" and chose to share her realm and blood.
Our Mother laid 100 eggs under the canopy of stars, and as the first Drakling awoke, she watched them break from their shells... and fed the weakest to the strong, so they may bring forth a storm of blood forevermore.

As the offspring of the Broodmother Vesztah, all of us strive for glory. Only the greatest rise into the land beyond the storm after death: Ark Morgo.

The first to embark on this journey was Merphisz. Hatched on a rocky shore, he was enamored by the waves from the beginning.

"These untamed waters shape the coastline, determine where life may sprout! I will overcome this ever-shifting spectre that haunts us so with its indifference and whim! I will sail to faraway shores and spread our seed, to make all blue synonymous with the mother's embrace!"

Shaped by the sea, he learned its language and began to understand its ebb and swell. Determined to usher his newly formed clan, the Drak'Mer, to fruitful shores, he set out towards the horizon — and found an archipelago nestled behind a fearsome storm.
Raising his trident, he challenged the taiphun to a duel, but lightning struck, and Merphisz's spirit was called to Ark Morgo. His clan reached the archipelago unscathed and holds dominion over the open waters still.

When told about the legend of Merphisz, Fyraszh sprung forth from the crowd of Drakling. 

"Why splash in water for eternity? Why adjust to the whims of the waves if you could forge your own path in fire?" He asked, red-hot with rage. Determination to surpass his brother swelled in him, so Fyraszh travelled not far, but deep. He set off to claim the core of the mountain, to forge his glory in molten metal and liquid heat. 

When they saw him again, his scales had hardened like coal, and the skin underneath glowed like the sun. Adorned in ash and gold, he yelled from the mountaintop: "See? The mountain rumbles and spouts, it chants our name and that of our clan! Drak' Fyr! Drak'Fyr!"

And as the mountain indeed sputtered and roared, a fountain as bright as the evening sun erupted behind him. The amber glow swallowed his body, but lifted his soul to Ark Morgo where he'd be a leader for all eternity.

The light of the bright, amber fountain coated the night sky as Arisztar hatched. He looked up above, and saw Fyraszh turn from flesh to fire.

"Why be confined to rocks and fiery rage?" Arisztar hushed. "To let yourself be swallowed by flames while so close to the clouds — That coward ought to jump! To fly where others fall is the greatest feat of all!"

So he took off and set his sights on the faraway cliffs. He lived high above the rest for years, hunting the birds, the vultures, and dragons above, until the Broodmother's spirit had blessed him with wings of his own. 
He became a leader unbound by the winds and soon commanded the clan of the Drak'Ari - but he would not be satisfied until he had truly soared higher than the rest. 

As he took a final leap of faith, he cried out: "Our land stretches as far as the winds blow! My wings will eclipse all below in their shadow!"
With these words, he flew closer to the sun. Silken feathers rained down as he entered Ark Morgo's halls.

The young Dalszul watched as feathers rained from the skies, leaving whispy shadows underneath them as they danced. 
He pondered: "What good is conquering the skies? The land is vast and rich with treasure! We ought to thrust towards the mainland and annihilate its core! Let its blood strengthen our soil and our bodies!

And so he sank his claws into the largest mass of land he could find, and formed blocks from clay and stone to build temples to his own glory. 
Countless Drak worked and died at his walls, and when his grandest monument was finished with its final brick, he laughed: "Broodmother, hear me now! Every stretch of land, from field to forest, squeals beneath my foot! My spear can point wherever the eye can see, and still spot no edge to my domain!

As he continued his tirade, unstoppable like a boulder rolling downhill, the Drak'Dal of his clan slowly backed away. They felt a rumble in the ground, and before they knew it, a large fracture before them ripped the Earth in two.
The monument beneath their leader's feet crumbled, and Dalszul was buried beneath the rubble and dust, his blood forever marking the heart of his territory. 
Ark Morgo had taken him.

Ancients. Yes. From Ark Morgo, they descend. Sent as messengers from gods. Vesztah! Merphisz! Fyraszh! Arisztar! Dalszul! To choose new gods, yes. The strongest among us!

But fools! Fools!
They choose humans! Weak Skulls, break easily! Squishy bellies, soft and flabby! Tiny fire-makers. Pah! Fire is weak. 
We stomp out spark, we swallow flame, we bring rise with storm of violet blood! 

But humans tricked us. Beat us in battle — with machines and devilry! Not fair! 

We bathed in shame and shadow for too long! Human flame is weak now! Should not burn near Ark Morgo! Their bodies are rotting. Bones soft, flesh spoiled — Time comes. Drak rise. Drak'Dal take chance in pitiful basin. Throne waits. Ark Morgo ours again!

Such big building! Tall spire! Bright light!

Can only be made by Descendants of Ark Morgo, yes — Ancients must be messengers! Connect to Ark Morgo above! Beam to the sky beyond the clouds! A pathway for the worthy! 

But glowy platform don't work right! Rah! 
Drak'Dal will prove themselves anyway! Will enter! Squish Flame in battle! Win favor of gods!

Large ship stranded on our shores.

Spoiled food, rotten wood. Merphisz would laugh at the state of it.

Clouds swirling around, misty blue like fog on the horizon, but murky. Humans inside, or something once human. Mushy and soft, rip open to reveal glowing hearts still beating in an unfamiliar rhythm. 

Weaklings! Ancients chose the wrong champions! Now is the time of the Drak! Drak'Dal will cross the open waters and squish the puny fleshlings! Rebuild the empire! 

For Dalszul!

Rah! Hunt over, many spoils!
Had Capybara snack. Bristles too tough. No like mouth feel. 

Chief Gna'Rash gets to eat supple, tiny one. Bristles soft. Fits well in mouth, one gulp. Squeaks when touched. Likes pets. But no time for pets! Time for feast! 

I challenge Gna'Rash: Eat squeaky baby whole. Maybe it makes Gna'Rash heavy and slow. Then Gruul can fight Gna'Rash! Become new chieftain! New elite! Later, become Hydrak! Eat all the squeaky babies myself! Claim better mouth feel! 
Rah Rah!

Gna'Rash's clutch grows well. Many strong Drakling. Only few need culling, but hide still strong. Tough for other Drakling to eat, but good nutrition. Makes scales twice as hard! Hail the Broodmother!

But why only Gna'Rash get to be with pretty Drak'Dal ladies? Gruul said chief even have girlfriends in Archipelago, outside tribe. Kriss'Kah wonder: How is breeding with Drak'Mer female? 
Why no pretty Drak ladies for Kriss'Kah? No fair!

lore.n: Note Of A Drak Hatchling Supervisor

p.t:
We need more daylilies for Drakling hatchery lamps.
Only fiery glow makes Drakling want to come out of egg.

Tha'Riel told me Drakling think it's sun on the horizon.
I hope they all hatch soon, before Kra'Thul comes and breaks eggs.

Awful bloodshed — so much cleaning.

Dra'Nak die with honor. 
So his claws, his scales, his blood — they go into totem. 
Old way of Drak. Always been. 
We keep the strong ones close — even when breath is gone. He stand with us, watch guard. 
Drak proud to become totem. Drak'Dal Chieftain will be Wood Totem, Hydrak'Dal Stone.
Means they will join Dalszul in afterlife. 
But if die with shame.. no gold, no name.. no afterlife... just forget.

Draconis Communis

Over 1000 years old
Embervale - Nomad Highlands; Umber Hollow

Dragons are perhaps the earliest known inhabitants of Embervale. Traces of their reign can still be discovered in the Nomad Highlands, the Kindlewastes, and the Albaneve Summits, from where they seem to originate. 
Our approximation of their origin and subsequent migratory patterns is based on the occurrence and density of ivory samples.

These winged and long-extinct giants are presumed to be the ancestors of Vultures, and perhaps even the Drak. 
The displayed specimen was discovered at the bottom of the once-water-filled Umber Hollow. It was retrieved from beneath the wing bones of a similar but larger and severely fractured skeleton, presumably damaged by meteorite impacts. It is due to this presumed sacrifice that the remains of our Common Dragon could be preserved and exhibited today.

Location: Embervale (East)

Climate: Dry, Arid. (Formerly: Lush.) 
Precipitation: No recent data.

Flora & Fauna: 
The Kindlewastes are a vast desert expanse of amber dunes and wind-swept plains. Though our kind would consider the local temperatures comfortable, they are interpreted as harsh and even hostile by local life forms.
Once a thriving, verdant ecosystem, the region now supports only the hardiest animals, including the elusive Dune Armadillo, carrion-feeding Draconian Vultures, and the ephemeral Humans.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Beneath the barren surface lies a wealth of natural resources, with deposits of iron, sulfur, lapis, and vast reserves of ancient ivory preserved beneath the sands. 

Summary: 
The Kindlewastes remain the largest terraforming experiment ever attempted, a monumental undertaking following the incident. Today, they stand as a testament to the rift between failure and success — and the resilience found within.

Location: Embervale (South West)

Climate: Continental, Mild 
Precipitation: Around 700 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
The welcoming wilds of the springlands harbor a plethora of ecological species. Temperatures in this biosphere remain relatively constant throughout the year, thereby facilitating the ideal conditions for a thriving, stable ecosystem.
Hophares and wolves are common wildlife sightings, but some Vukah tribes have recently settled here, too. Berries, mushrooms, and tomatoes create the basis of every herbivore's diet.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Resource variety is seemingly poor. Only common minerals and rocks, such as salt and flintstone, can be obtained here.

Summary: 
The verdant fields of the Springlands are considered pleasant and quiet by most. Due to their temperate nature and well-preserved biodiversity, they serve as a still frame of a perfectly balanced habitat.

Location: Embervale (Mid-West)

Climate: Continental, Humid
Precipitation: Around 1200 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
This biosphere is rich in a variety of hardwood species and wildlife. The thick underbrush and dense canopy deserve special attention, as they shelter countless insects, and most notably, arachnids.
Alongside the many muddied pathways, strawberries, chamomile, flax, and indigo plants foster a fragrant and colorful environment. Despite this enticing pull of the bosque, it is advised not to wander off the pathways. Boars roam in the forest, aggressively defending their farrowing nests and young.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Alongside the many mossy cliff faces, wanderers are likely to find bright orange deposits of clay, copper, and, at lower levels, amber.

Summary: 
The overgrown wilds of the Revelwood teem with life and mystery. Anyone brave enough to venture off the beaten path will be able to find proverbial "pearls" in the mud. Still, it is imperative not to be caught off guard by sudden rainfall or hungry, feral pigs.

Location: Embervale (Centre)

Climate: Semi-arid
Precipitation: Around 350 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
Plant growth here is limited to select areas wherein the ground can retain adequate moisture. Within the pale green fields that dot the Nomad Highlands, travellers may encounter sugar cane and bell pepper plants, as well as Flightless Redtails, which feed on their seeds.
The local birdlife produces nutritious eggs, which serve as excellent sources of protein for the primary predators: Sabertooth Tigers and Humans.

Geological & Mineral Data 
The region presents both flat plains and staggering differences in altitude. The biosphere is undercut with an underground river network that converges on a former lake (Umber Hollow), which was caused by a large meteorite impact. 

Summary: 
The Highlands are equidistant to both the Revelwood and the Kindlewastes — serving as a transitional space between the very humid and extensively dry climates, respectively. The central location and easily traveled upper layer have elevated the area to a bustling trade hub that hides many riches in the forgotten caverns below.

Location: Embervale (North East)

Climate: Alpine
Precipitation: From 500 mm (leeward) to 2000 mm (windward)

Flora & Fauna:
The frigid summits are defined by low to sub-zero temperatures, which cover the local peaks in thick layers of snow. Below the frost, only a few species dare to thrive. Yaks have proven resilient to the climate due to their insulating coat of fur. Their biggest adversary is not the cold, but the Cyclops that roam the bluffs looking for a feast to roast.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Many rare earths and minerals can be found in the mountains. Red marble, amethyst, and even ancient deposits of obsidian hide deep within the rock. 

Summary: 
The freezing cold of the summits is considered unpleasant, if not hostile, by most lifeforms (especially ours!) Still, between snow-covered fields and the aurora borealis dancing above, life persists.

Location: Embervale (North West)

Climate: Tropical, Marine
Precipitation: Around 3000 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
The Veilwater Basin is characterized by crystal lakes and lush ecological variety. The rivulets teem with fish, and docile species such as the capybara can be encountered enjoying bananas and coconuts by the shore.
Despite this bliss, considerable dangers lurk below the water. The Basin was previously home to the Drak'Dal, a subspecies or tribe of the Drak. Their temples and altars may be no more than flooded ruins, but as a highly territorial species, they may eventually attempt to reclaim their old hunting grounds.

Geological & Mineral Data 
The coastal region is rich with gold, nacre, and pearls. Unfortunatly, many resources are buried beneath the water's surface, requiring eager gatherers to expose themselves to the elements.

Summary: 
The Veilwater Basin may appear like a paradise at first, but its foreboding history may yet reveal a dark future. Nevertheless, the area remains a fascinating botanical playground with an endless amount of genetic material to probe.

p.n: Field Notes — Day 8 of Yearwake, 509 D.A.
p.t:
Rimgard's soldiers are good for one thing, at least. After they broke through the Ancient barrier, I was able to slip past.  If they could break the seal here, they most likely managed to surmount the gate, as well...

Lord Vorgoth must already be on his way. Right now, it's just a thesis... but not without circumstantial evidence:
The Shroud has gathered here in unprecedented levels. It creeps from the Veilwater Basin all the way through to... where, exactly? Some central point, a platform I can spy far below.... right beneath the floating isles. 

I am not alone in my quest to ascend. Rotting tendrils stretch upward, clawing at the 
drifting land rafts above — keeping them low. And therefore, within even my reach.

As long as the Shroud's attention is away from this platform, there may still be time. I have to take my chances.

— Loraine Crim

p.n: Field Notes — Day 26 of Yearwake, 509 D.A.
p.t:
I've felt this heat before. 

Long ago, I left my assistant Nala to research a monument within the Pillars of Creation... a strange, portal-like structure amid a sea of flame.
She called it a "gateway"— a jest, I know. And yet: Perhaps she was right. And perhaps... this platform could be similar: A teleporter to the isles above.

Of course, it's not activated. That would be too easy, wouldn't it?
Two observations:
1. I see pillars of light in the distance, aligned with the directions of the markers that surround the platform.

2. These pillars may be akin to the beacons of the Ancient Spires, and must be conquered to power the teleporter! 

...Let's add a third remark, for good measure:
3. My provisions are running low. I cannot, should not leave this platform. 

I wonder what Nala or Fran would say if they could see me now: On the other side of the world, the edge of eternity, reaching for the stars while being chained to a pit.

It seems I only learnt the language of the Ancients to understand a single, cruel joke. In fact, I may have become the punchline.

Well, we'll see who gets the last laugh. I still have hope. I always will.

We had long run out of any meaningful medicine when we captured the injured Ancient. There was nothing that I could have done for it, even if I had wanted to.

Stitching up the walking, bloated corpses around me had used up every bandage. Suturing their ruptured organs shut — or in place — had cost us all thread. For me to dull the thrumming of my own head, well, I had emptied every Elixer flask I'd brought.

So as the Ancient lay dying, all I could do was watch. So watch I did, as it crumbled betwixt my fingers, turned gray, and fell to ash.

It was so peculiar.
When you lose patients — human ones — you close their eyes, bury their bodies, and visit their overgrown graves once or twice. 
But when an Ancient dies, it fades from the world. After an eternity on Embervale, all they leave is dust. There is nothing to bury, really. Nothing to mourn.

My head's pounding again. Should've brought more Elixir...

The council may be divided, but it matters not. We must ascend. There is no other choice.

It seems our youngest member plans to leave the council.
To split from both the council and the Mother Flame's embrace at one's own behest is, of course, an ignominy — and even worse: entirely witless.

As soon as Ezramin departs, we will count the votes anew — and the outcome will be clear as day. Then, we will route our energy to the Mother Flame to fuel our ascent... but whether or not it will be enough, none can say.

We suffer from stagnation.
A new flavor, I admit — though a bittersweet one at best.

We don't possess enough energy to fuel our ascent. 

Therefore, we remain in the interim; suspended above the grime and dirt — reaching for the fruit of the stars, hands bound.

We are ripped apart. And as such, we will remain.
Corporally, spiritually...

When we are only half, then we are not enough.

Maybe we will never be.

We've no more fuel to burn, and the Shroud has reached our abode.
We could not run. Could not hide. We were a harvest, ripe for picking.

For the first time in centuries, an Ancient has died by the blade — severed from the Mother Flame's light... trying desperately to stall the worms, the tendrils, the rot.

A fruitless venture, of course. 

We should not die as shields. We should die as fuel... to buy time. To flee. To save what matters most.
We will be the energy — until our bodies can be reshaped, until our souls are reborn... if ever.
There is no other way.

The excavation was successful. The following analysis — not so much.

I was there when we uncovered the cave room. Finding it was easy, for it made its presence known from the moment we broke ground. Fine tendrils crept across the stone like vines, spindly and thin at first, then thicker and sluggish further down. They outlined a path all the way to the heart.

First inspection would lead one to believe that what lingers before us is a large, decomposing fungal root... yet, what shows up under the microscope is anything but. 

The organism is alive, still. Undying, and refusing to be analysed or understood. It re-shapes itself upon being observed, latching onto nearby cells and matter, consuming, mimicking, changing them. It is utterly fascinating.

Such properties hold great potential! We ought to dig deeper, push further — perhaps these roots could hold the secret to a longer life... to eternity, even!

- Manathor; Expedition Lead

The root has been more "active" as of late, reacting to the stimuli around it as if awoken. According to the enclosing rock formations and their geological records, this organism may have slumbered for thousands of years. However, we may not be its first guests. 
While it refuses to be catalogued properly, it always holds to a similar core; a codex of matter that appears entirely external — not mycelial or plant-like. Not human. Not Ancient, either. Whatever it is, it was absorbed in bygone ages, therefore predating our records.

Its past is riveting, but so is its future. We've distilled the roots into a liquid — a shimmering blue Elixir, captivating and serene — and stored it for further testing.

Surprisingly, it was gone when I walked by storage today. No signs of unpermitted intrusion... Only a scrap of dark, tattered fabric in the rubble. I was worried until a belated order for inventory transfer arrived. My assistants must have re-organized samples ahead of schedule.

The dead skincells on the fabric present with the same matter codex as the fungal roots, so the scrap was likely here all along. I wonder what existed first: The root, or the lifeform sampled by it?

- Manathor; Expedition Lead

Summary: 
A fungal organism composed of transformative cells capable of adhering to and consuming organic matter. Assimilated material is either replicated or altered into novel biological structures.

Properties: 
Mycelial. Dormant. Feeds on organic matter. 

Research Category: 
Medicinal; Longevity.

Research Note: 
Growth appears cyclical rather than linear. The organism may exist in a perpetual sequence of expansion, bloom, decay, and renewal. Further observation is required to determine whether these phases are environmentally triggered or intrinsic to its biology.

p.n: Test Subject No. 73 - Distilled Fungal Root Liquid
p.t:
Summary: 
An emissive liquid derived from distilled fungal roots (see Test Subject No. 72 ).

Proporties: 
Emotionally invigorating. Analgesic. Habit-forming.

Research Category: 
Medicinal; Longevity.

Research Note: 
Concerning side effects. Long-term impact study required.
________
NEW: Subject was relocated after a request for inventory transfer.

To improve traversal between the smaller splitter islands, we have begun establishing a series of directed air currents — stable upstreams intended to serve as fixed transit corridors across the Ancient Land.
Navigation along these routes is aided considerably by the Signal Blocks, which emit a strong enough light to remain visible at great distance, including low-visibility conditions such as overcast weather or night time. They function well as orientation markers.
Additional Signal Blocks are stored on an island beyond our current range. The air currents are not yet calibrated to support passage that far out.

We tried to rise. To escape. To save ourselves — to save the Mother Flame. But we are stuck. Something's got a hold of us, and we all know too well what it is.
The plan now is to go into the flame. That is all we have left. And the others – they are grabbing things. Their most prized possessions. I don't know what they think will come out of it. Maybe they don't know either. But their panic is spreading and I feel it now too.
The only thing I have left of real value are the full golden building blocks. They're much too heavy. I have to leave them behind and just hope.
I am going in as I am. Knowledge is the only thing worth carrying anyway. Everything else is just weight.

(But just in case, I hid them close by but out of sight. So when I come back, something is waiting for me)

The site handles the extraction of raw minerals and metals from the surrounding deposits. Once pulled, material is sorted and loaded at the transport station for shipment to processing locations elsewhere. Flow has been steady — no major holdups.

Left-over building blocks from our tower restoration are being held in the storage area adjacent to the mining site for now. It keeps them close to transit and out of the way of active extraction.

Members Present
Listed in order of seniority: Manathor, Eldermere, Claravinta, Ezramin.

Topic 1: Ecological Impact of Botanical Alteration

Ongoing alterations to the composition of local flora have demonstrated additional effects on wildlife populations.

Motion:
That all botanical research activities be suspended.

Vote:
Unanimous opposition. Motion denied.

Notes:
Elder Claravinta proposed limiting future experimentation to controlled greenhouse environments to minimize unintended ecological impact.

Topic 2: Observatory Operations and Resource Allocation

Work in the observatory continues, but progress has plateaued.

Motion:
That additional resources be allocated to interstellar charting efforts to better identify viable routes.

Vote:
Unanimous approval. Motion carried.

Notes:
None.

Topic 3: Human Contact with the Elixir
Humanity has discovered the Elixir. How this came about remains unknown. Consequences are expected to be unfavorable.

Motion:
That the council maintains noninterference.

Vote:
Inconclusive. Deliberation postponed.

Notes:
This constitutes the first inconclusive vote recorded in recent council history.
Council member Ezramin expressed strong opposition during proceedings and was subsequently asked to withdraw from the chamber.

p.n: Ancients aren't born. We are salvaged.
p.t:
The Mother Flame grants us life. She lets us walk the Earth in search of wisdom and discovery — and when we return to her, carrying our gifts, she takes it back. For a time, at least.

Therefore, Ancient souls, or sparks, are limited. They linger in the light, connected to all that came before, and all that will ever be, until expelled anew — wiped clean. 

This cycle is holy. Its purity is beyond reproach. 

But a spark alone cannot be. It is merely a consciousness, a soul, a memory core in need of a host. To house a spark, we require a shell. Shells are disposable. They crumble to dust as our end draws near, not meant to be mourned.

Should we perish outside the Flame's grasp — an unlikely event, as we reign eternal — then we are lost, until returned to her light.

- Manathor

Once upon a time, the Mother Flame produced a spark every solstice. Now, we are lucky to receive "offspring" once a decade. Our numbers have dwindled ever since our youngest began to meddle with humanity.

This is most shameful. A mark on our pride and neutrality.
To waste one's life — to leave the circle, to forsake the mother's embrace in the name of something so laughable as empathy... is pitiful. 

But still, I must admit... As the eldest, I can feel the Mother Flame's pull, but uncertainty plagues me, so I, too, refuse her call.

Because it hasn't always been like this, has it?
The voices in the Flame, echoes through space and time, speak of fathers. Brothers. Sons. Of families and origins that were unbound, unrenewable... but their whispers all bleed together, chained as one. 

We used to be born. We used to die. We used to be remembered.
So, how calcified is our journey? How forgettable, how memorable may I be?
...And how wrong, how true, how unchangeable are we, really?

- Manathor

I present herewith my findings on our cultivation project, prepared in accordance with the Council's decree.

My observations can be summarized as follows:

The ferns exhibit healthy growth and development, continuing to improve overall air quality. Efforts to increase the climate resilience of Bloomhearts through the implementation of a protective petal overcoat have borne fruit — No jest intended.

Analysis of the latest harvest indicates no significant reduction in quality. The fruit's flavor profile remains consistent with that of earlier specimens.

Based on these findings, the project can be considered a success. Continued observation is recommended to assess long-term stability and performance.

Capacity remains limited. We may consider moving further experimentation efforts to our post in the Revelwood.

Elder Claravinta

The new seed storage sector is coming to fruition. Once completed, the conservatory will have the capacity to preserve genetic material for secondary — and potentially tertiary — ecological projects, expanding the scope of future restorative or evolutionary initiatives.

Near endless possibilities are blossoming before us... No pun intended. Yet, I find our side projects most riveting. The ongoing development of the Fig'23 flavor profile presents several promising avenues for culinary use.
Through cultivating a mutated strand, we can make the fruit prickly, sour, and sweet on the tongue. I'm thinking of calling it "Prickle Pearl". 

Each discovery opens another path for exploration, but while there is much we know, there's far more we don't. The work continues.

Elder Claravinta

Construct pipeline status is satisfactory. Approval for large-scale production has been granted for the following models:

Worker Constructs
M.I.N.R. - Metallurgical, Industrial and Nonmetal extraction Rig (3rd gen.)
B.L.D.R. - Building, Landscaping, and Demolition Rig (3rd gen.)
G.T.H.R. - Grunt Transportation and Hauling Rig (2nd gen.)

Security Constructs
S.I.R.N. - Signal and Intrusion Reveal Node (Includes: Static, Mobile)

Combat Constructs
G.A.R.D. - Guarding and high Alert Resolution Defender (Includes: Burner, Slicer, and Dozer variant)
G.U.N.R. - Gunnery and Ultrasonic Neutron Rocketcore (Includes: Short, Medium, Long Ranged variant)

Approval remains pending for the following models:

Security
C.R.T.R. - Construct Reconstruction and Termination Rig 
Findings: The C.R.T.R. fulfills its duties as a small maintenance and reconstruction unit, but it does not reliably terminate faulty constructs.

The following model has not been approved for mass production:

Security
S.P.D.R. - Security Patrol Dome Rig
Findings: The S.P.D.R. continues to demonstrate far too significant destructive potential when operating in an alarm state.

- Artificer Constantio

Construct rigs were exchanged successfully. The Worker's Ward is now fully equipped with 3rd-generation models. Please find additional information attached below.

Worker Constructs
M.I.N.R.
The new Metallurgical, Industrial, and Nonmetal extraction Rigs have elevated efficiency by about 34%. This productivity increase is largely attributable to the Archaic Core additions, which enable new models to recharge at Charge Stations.

G.T.H.R.
New Grunts (Transportation and Hauling Rigs) were deployed. The process of gathering, transporting, and storing sediment and ore has been streamlined.

C.R.T.R.
The Construct Reconstruction and Termination Rigs were deployed for improved rig maintenance.

Results are satisfactory. Implementation approved.
Seeing as this report is finished, I'll withdraw to my chambers once more to conclude my own research — please do not disturb me. The entry is concealed for a reason.

- Artificer Constantio

My findings on the Andromeda's Eye telescope are as follows:

Objective Lens, Star Diagonal, Eyepiece - Working as intended.

Optical Tube Assembly - Working as intended, but dusty. Should we send a student to aid in cleaning...?

Mount - Error detected. The Telescope does not move horizontally or perpendicularly. 

Focusing Components - Working as intended, though they cause me great misery nevertheless — Seeing as they can only reveal the constellations directly up ahead.

Conclusion: Consider conducting a proper maintenance routine.

- Professor Androme

During my absence, I expect you, my young star explorers, to consider the following assignment! Solve it to lift the seal — and to earn a good grade!

Imagine your life as a circle. 
It can be a halo, bright and hollow — or an interlocking chain; an oroboros. Mind you: The emptiness, the vastness in between, is valuable. It serves as a canvas upon which we may draw our constellations and mark the flow of time, separating what is from that which isn't.

You spring from the inside of the circle — poof, there you are! A novice, young and spry, undulating along the proposed curvature, aging into elderhood and falling to ash before sprouting anew. 

Your task: Use the telescopes on the balconies to discover where, on this eternal cycle, our beginning and our end must lie!

To the left, I want you to find our origin — where we were plucked from the void and thrown onto the canvas. The point of our creation!

On the right side, focus on where we rest — the hearth that rekindles our ashes!

I await your results with bated breath!
- Professor Androme

The master's riddle is a tedious one... A circle has no end, nor beginning! Though the more I think on it, I begin to see all the hints he strew between the lines... in the empty space below, on the canvas, so to speak!

So my theory is as follows:
As Ancients, we all spring from the Mother Flame... but strangely, only one of the telescopes can be pointed towards where she resides. Perhaps part of the riddle is meant in a less literal way? Does the master refer to an "arrival", rather than a birth? 
I think his remark towards "creation" could prove valuable...

I'll try my luck with the telescopes and see!

Vorgoth is coming, and he's bringing his army.

The barrier, already weakened from our energy redistribution and ascent, has been breached.
We cannot run — we have to rise before it's too late!

The sky is our only escape... Only there can the Mother Flame be safe!

It has to work. It simply must...

Humans have, amongst other things, one very interesting habit. They "dream".

Dreaming; verb, is defined as an involuntary action that is subconsiously undertaken during sleep. Dreams, that is, the mental imagery proceedings that present themselves before the dreamer; noun, may have different qualities and therefore, offer a great variety and enrichment.

They can be frightening — see subcategory "nightmares"  — entertaining, confusing, or soothing. Dreams may present their own internal logic, which is often parallel but not at all analogous to that of the waking world.

I've been meaning to engage with this human tradition for a while, but as I lie down to rest, I find it difficult to conjure a dream. I followed all the known steps: 
My eyes were closed. I pretended to count all sorts of woolly animals — although none were around. Still, the strange, flickering scenes would not cross my vision. "Dreams" seem to elude us Ancients entirely. 

I may need to investigate the subcategory of "Day Dreaming" instead.

There is one specific recreational activity that humans seem to "dream" of before, or during, sleep.

Through all depictions (of which there are many), I've gathered that it seems to be some... mostly unclothed coital gymnastic tandem operation?

I've decided to try my hand at the courting process that traditionally precedes this act. I wonder if a human would consider this flattering?

Your human skin is as smooth as silk — the most adequate texture imaginable. My ear holes do not mind enduring the sound of your voice, which is, sonically speaking, like honey to me (in a purely metaphorical way). Your immediate proximity increases my body temperature to levels that lie just below those of the common fever, which is, somehow, not concerning, but in fact, very enticing. Above all, I most enjoy the way your hips sway so very rhythmically.

It seems the lyrical pull these words ought to have still eludes me... still, penning them was at least somewhat amusing.

Humans have flames, as do we. 
They use fire to forge bonds, to light the dark, and to destroy. It can be summarized as the source of all their inventions; all their progress. Our Flame is not so unlike theirs.

Humans eat fruit and drink wine, as do we.
In fact, we've only adopted these customs due to humanity's influence — a factor often forgotten all too willingly.

Humans gaze at the stars, as do we.
We are all under the same skies. The same constellations. They've shown us their suspicion and wrath, but also their tremendous kindness — especially the people of Orindell.

Are we so different after all? Ought we to preserve a kind of hollow sanctity, only because we are hundreds, and they are millions? Because we lay claim to endlessness? I think not. I think we share more than we care to admit. And shouldn't that mean that we ought to stand beside them, rather than judge from above?

Embervale belongs to all of us.
- Ezramin

The gateway to the Albaneve Summits research lab is finished.

This may well be by far the least favored biosphere... the freezing air makes it difficult to draw from any fire; any energy around. I much prefer the calming heat of the Cradle. It's simply so invigorating!

Humanity seems to avoid the cold, too — though some also revel in its briskness, and the challenge those lonely mountains in particular provide. 
Most curious. There may be a hidden charm to the snow that I have not yet discovered. Perhaps constructing a snowpal would aid me in my quest of understanding!

Humans have hair. Not a single strand, of course, nor matted long coats of fur — no! They have tufts of it, mostly (but not exclusively!) atop their slightly oblong marble heads.

It can be long, short, curly, straight, blond, red, pitch black, and so many other curious things! Some are blessed with very healthy, youthful manes, while others must prematurely kiss their locks goodbye — revealing said glistening egglike domes. In conclusion, there are as many facets of hair as there are humans themselves!

I find this incredibly fascinating... but if the others discover my juvenile interests, they may send me back to the Mother Flame immediately!

What to do, what to do...

The constructs are simple, straightforward creations with linear purpose and ability. The MINR drones deployed here, for example, were equipped with diamond-tipped drills. This enables them to operate, when used in tandem with Charge Stations, nearly indefinitely.

Despite their efficacy, they're dull. Mindless husks fueled by an unrelenting flow of energy, and entirely interchangeable.

We Ancients are different. Our souls, gifts from the Flame, hold our minds. They are finite and delicate, carefully granted to our similarly "constructed" bodies in Proto Vessels. The corpus serves as a shell that contains the spark, imbuing us with warmth and light.

I find these connections between "body/mind" or "mechanical/ephemeral" most fascinating, but I wonder... could the power of the Flame grant ability, even if it were inverted? 

The answer I discovered is this Eternal Ice Arrow — but the coldness it exudes is deeply unpleasant to me, so I may set it aside for now.

Both recharge stations and model rigs are in order, though the terminal seems uncharacteristically untidy and crowded — but I suppose the residents tend more to the greenhouse than to construct maintenance. 
Elder Claravinta really only focuses on whatever occupies her mind most. It's very "human" of her, I fear.

That reminds me: Recent proximity to humanity has inspired me to come up with a new invention! A model suit, meant to combine my construct research with the agile, human frame — bipedal, and somewhat compressed to fit the strange proportions these stubby animals possess.

Perhaps this venture will one day bring forth a new era for our constructs, or the Ancients at large!
